thread.title: Apple: Here’s Why Services Are So Important

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: Here’s Why Services Are So Important
text:
Photo: TIMOTHY A. CLARY/AFP/Getty Images While many investors are focused on device sales at Apple and other tech companies, services could be the way forward as the company tries to work its way toward a $ 1 trillion market cap . 
“Over the last five years, the vast majority (86%) of Apple’s 8% annual revenue growth was driven by iPhone sales ,” Morgan Stanley analysts wrote in a Thursday note. “But as replacement cycles extend further and device installed base growth slows to single digits (from 14% over the last two years), it is through monetization of Apple’s (AAPL) Services business that we see the company still generating mid single digit revenue growth.”
Morgan Stanley, which has a $203 price target—about 21% above current levels—on the Barron’s Next 50 stock’s shares, suggested several “levers” the company could use to accomplish this. (Related: Here’s one columnist’s view on services we covered last month—the idea of “ Apple Prime .”)
Illustration: Morgan Stanley • Apple Music, which the analysts said was growing subscribers “slightly faster than peers” but still has lots of room to expand;
• iCloud, which is growing subscribers “even faster than Apple Music” and recently announced two Chinese data centers that could “drive increasing user penetration”;
• Apple Pay, which is widely available in retail locations but suffers from low usage; and
•the App Store, where “broadening payment options can accelerate demand”; original content and augmented reality apps could “convert new users and increase spend of existing services users,” they wrote
Meanwhile, the analysts wrote, Apple has dedicated resources to decreasing subscriber churn.
